# Reading Telemetry & Observability \- Participant Lab Guide: Day 3

## Hands-On Production Scenarios, Troubleshooting & Resolution Guidelines

### Splunk, Dynatrace & Datadog Query Languages

---

## 1\. Module-Wise Setup Requirements

The three Day 3 scenarios are **independent**. Each one has its own setup, its own platform and its own sign-off. You can do them in any order, and none of them needs another one to be running.

| Scenario | Platform | How it runs | What you set up |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **S1 TEL-D3-301** | Splunk Enterprise (trial) | **Local Docker** on your machine | Docker \+ one command (Section 1.1) |
| **S2 TEL-D3-302** | Dynatrace Grail (DQL) | **Browser**, easyTravel on the shared EC2 host | Nothing to install; instructor starts the fault |
| **S3 TEL-D3-303** | Datadog Monitors | **Browser**, easyTravel on the shared EC2 host | Nothing to install; instructor starts the fault |

### 1.1 S1 Setup: Local Docker (Splunk)

| Item | Requirement | How to Check |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **OS** | Ubuntu 20.04+/macOS/Windows 10-11 (Docker Desktop) | \- |
| **Docker \+ Compose v2** | Docker 24+ | `docker compose version` |
| **Resources** | 4 GB free RAM, 6 GB free disk | Docker Desktop \> Resources |
| **Port** | `8000` free (Splunk Web) | Nothing else listening on 8000 |
| **Python (optional)** | 3.8+; if missing the script uses a Docker Python image | `python3 --version` |

Start the incident (first run downloads the Splunk image, about 1 GB, and takes 5-10 minutes):

```sh
# Ubuntu / Linux / macOS:
cd reading_telemetry/day3/s1
./validation_script.sh start

# Windows PowerShell:
cd reading_telemetry\day3\s1
.\validation_script.ps1 start
```

The script generates the logs for the last 4 hours, starts the container `tel-d3-301-splunk`, creates the indexes `retail_web` and `retail_checkout` and loads the data. Open `http://localhost:8000` (user `admin`, password printed by the script). After about 1 minute, `index=retail_* earliest=-4h | stats count by index` must show `retail_checkout 3000` and `retail_web 2400`. When you are finished run `./validation_script.sh reset` (Windows: `.\validation_script.ps1 reset`).

### 1.2 S2 and S3 Setup: Browser Only

You install nothing, run no terminal command, start no Docker container and open no local port. The instructor runs the incident on the shared EC2 host `ip-172-30-0-220` (easyTravel) and announces the start time.

| Item | Requirement | How to Check |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Browser** | Current Chrome or Firefox | Open the platform URL below |
| **Seat number** | `u01` to `u40` (from your instructor) | Used in names |
| **Evidence file** | One per scenario (Word / Google Doc / the supplied file) | Instructor shares the copy |
| **Screen capture** | Any screenshot tool | Attach screenshots to the evidence |

&nbsp;

| Platform | Address | Access Model |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Dynatrace** (S2) | `https://xiz79164.apps.dynatrace.com` | Cohort group; can create own Notebooks |
| **Datadog** (S3) | `https://app.datadoghq.com` (organisation KloudKraft, `env:cohort`) | Cohort login; own monitors only |

### 1.3 Rules for the Shared Environment (S2, S3)

- Read, search, filter and screenshot as much as you like. **Never** close, mute, edit or delete shared problems, monitors, dashboards or other learners' objects.  
- Name anything you create with your seat prefix (`u<seat>_` or `[u<seat>]`). Monitors notify nobody, or only your own e-mail.  
- Always use a time filter (for example Last 2 hours). Do not paste credentials into screenshots or evidence files.

---

## 2\. Common Instructions for Trainers and Participants

### Standard Scenario Workflow

1. Read the ticket (Story and Expected Failure) and `starter/README_START_HERE.txt` of your scenario.  
2. **S1:** run the start script (Section 1.1). **S2 and S3:** wait for the instructor to announce the start time and write it in your evidence file.  
3. Investigate with the Investigation Guidelines. Paste the **exact query or screen path** you used and screenshots.  
4. Fill every field of the evidence file (no `<<FILL_...>>` left).  
5. **S1:** run `./validation_script.sh check` for a self-check. **S2 and S3:** the instructor signs you off against the 5 rules in Section 4 in the browser.  
6. Clean up: S1 `reset`; S3 delete your monitors (composite first).

### Where Things Are (Same Folder Structure as Before)

Each scenario folder (`s1/`, `s2/`, `s3/`) keeps `starter/README_START_HERE.txt`, `starter/evidence/` and a `validation_script`. In S1 the script is yours (start, check, reset). In S2 and S3 it is an instructor-only helper; you do not run it.

## 3\. Day 3: Splunk, Dynatrace & Datadog Query Languages

### Scenario TEL-D3-301: Error Spike on One Host After a Release

- **Ticket ID:** `TEL-D3-301` \| **Category:** Log Analytics & Advanced SPL \| **Suggested Time:** 90 mins  
- **Platform:** Splunk in local Docker \| **Evidence:** `starter/evidence/evidence_D3_1.md`

#### The Story

A release two hours ago was followed by an error spike on the ShopNow retail web tier. Operations report that the error rate after the deployment rose to 8.4 %. Standard log searches do not extract the unstructured error codes from the application logs. You are assigned to find which host is responsible, extract and chart the error codes, and find the long, failing sessions.

#### A. Expected Failure (What You Should See)

1. Run the start script and open `http://localhost:8000`.

![][image1]

2. In Search & Reporting set the time range to **Last 4 hours** and search `index=retail_checkout`. There is no `err_code` field: the code is hidden in the raw text as `status_code=ERR-4011`.

![][image2]

3. **Observed:** the error rate after the release is 8.4 % and a plain search cannot group the errors by code.

![][image3]

#### B. Step-by-Step Investigation Guidelines

- **Action:** Host breakdown: `(index=retail_web OR index=retail_checkout) earliest=-4h | stats count by host, sourcetype | sort -count`.

![][image4]

- **Action:** Isolate the culprit host: `web-prod-04` produces about 92 % of the errors.

![][image5]

- **Action:** Extract the codes with a regex: `rex field=_raw "status_code=(?<err_code>ERR-[0-9]{4})"`.

![][image6]

- **Action:** Chart them every 15 minutes: `timechart span=15m count by err_code`.

![][image7]

&nbsp;

- **Action:** Group sessions: `index=retail_checkout earliest=-4h | transaction session_id maxspan=30m | where duration > 10 | table session_id, duration, eventcount`.

![][image8]

![][image9]

- **Action:** Complete `evidence_D3_1.md`.

![][image10]

#### C. Action Items to Solve

1. Record the culprit host and the share of errors it produces.

![][image5]

2. Paste the rex and timechart queries and the codes you found.

![][image11]

3. Paste the transaction query and the number of sessions longer than 10 seconds.

![][image12]

![][image13]

4. State the likely root cause (a bad release on one host) and the next action.

![][image14]

5. Run `./validation_script.sh check` (Windows `.\validation_script.ps1 check`), then call your instructor.

![][image15]

&nbsp;

### Scenario TEL-D3-302: Which App Is Failing? Ask Grail

- **Ticket ID:** `TEL-D3-302` \| **Category:** Log & Metric Analytics \| **Suggested Time:** 75 mins  
- **Platform:** Dynatrace only (browser) \| **Evidence:** `starter/evidence/evidence_D3_2.md`

#### The Story

Checkout on easyTravel (shared EC2 host `ip-172-30-0-220`, OneAgent) fails and several processes log errors at the same time. A plain log search cannot tell you which process fails or which error type dominates. Using only Dynatrace Notebooks and DQL, find the failing process and the dominant error type.

#### A. Expected Failure (What You Should See)

1. Open `https://xiz79164.apps.dynatrace.com` and sign in.

![][image16]

2. Open **Logs** with the time range **Last 2 hours**. ERROR lines from the easyTravel processes are mixed together.

![][image17]

3. **Observed:** many ERROR lines; one error text, `CreditCardCheckError500`, keeps repeating. Nothing in the list tells you which process produces most of them.

![][image18]

![][image19]

&nbsp;

&nbsp;

&nbsp;

&nbsp;

&nbsp;

&nbsp;

#### B. Step-by-Step Investigation Guidelines

- **Action:** Apps \> Notebooks \> New notebook, name it `u<seat>_TEL-D3-302`. Add a DQL section.  
- ![][image20]

&nbsp;

- **Action:** Start from `conf/grail_query_starter.dql` and write the Grail pipeline: `fetch logs, from: now() - 2h | filter loglevel == "ERROR" | fieldsAdd` `error_type = if(contains(content, "CreditCardCheckError500"), "CreditCardCheckError500", else: "other") | summarize ErrorCount = count(), by: {dt.process.name, error_type} | sort ErrorCount desc`.  
- ![][image21]  
- **Action:** Identify the top failing process and the dominant error type.

![][image22]

![][image23]

- **Action:** Failed requests by service: `fetch spans, from: now() - 2h | filter request.is_failed == true | summarize failed = count(), by: {service.name} | sort failed desc`.

![][image24]

- **Action:** Chart failures:timeseries failures \= sum(dt.service.request.failure\_count), by: {dt.smartscape.service}, from: now() \- 2h  
- \| fieldsAdd service \= getNodeName(dt.smartscape.service)  
- &nbsp;![][image25]  
- **Action:** Cross-check: in the **Logs** app filter `content` for `CreditCardCheckError500` (same 2 hours) and compare the count with your Notebook count.

![][image26]

![][image27]

- **Action:** Complete `evidence_D3_2.md`.  
- ![][image28]

#### C. Action Items to Solve

1. Paste the exact DQL of the log summary and the top three rows (process, error type, ErrorCount).

![][image29]

2. Name the top failing process and the dominant error type.

![][image30]

![][image31]

3. Paste the failed-span and timeseries results, and say whether they point to the same service.

![][image32]

![][image33]

&nbsp;

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;4\.  Record both counts of the cross-check and explain any small difference (timing, filter).

![][image34]

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;5\. cick the 5 self-check boxes and call your instructor.

![][image35]

### Scenario TEL-D3-303: The Error Monitor That Never Fires

- **Ticket ID:** `TEL-D3-303` \| **Category:** Alert Configuration \| **Suggested Time:** 75 mins  
- **Platform:** Datadog only (browser) \| **Evidence:** `starter/evidence/evidence_D3_3.json`

#### The Story

Checkout on easyTravel is failing, and `CreditCardCheckError500` appears in the logs, yet the shared monitor `[SHARED][BROKEN] easyTravel Backend Errors (TEL-D3-303)` stays green or shows No Data. Find out why it never fires, build a correct monitor and add a composite that pages only when the symptom and the known cause are both present.

#### A. Expected Failure (What You Should See)

1. Open `https://app.datadoghq.com`, time range **Past 1 Hour**.  
2. Open **Monitors \> Manage Monitors** and find `[SHARED][BROKEN] easyTravel Backend Errors (TEL-D3-303)`.  
3. **Observed:** status OK or No Data while **Logs** with `env:cohort service:easytravel-backend "CreditCardCheckError500"` shows errors.

#### B. Step-by-Step Investigation Guidelines

- **Action:** Open the broken monitor and record its query: `avg(last_5m):avg:trace.servlet.request.errors{env:staging,service:easytravel-backend} > 50` (also in `conf/datadog_monitor_broken.json`).  
- **Action:** Identify the two defects: (1) `env:staging` instead of `env:cohort` (it watches an environment with no data), (2) an average of a raw error count with a fixed threshold of 50 instead of an error ratio that works at any traffic level.  
- **Action:** Prove defect 1 in **Metrics Explorer**: graph the broken query (no data), then the same query with `env:cohort` (data appears).  
- **Action:** Create monitor A in the UI: **Monitors \> New Monitor \> Metric**, use the Source toggle, and paste `sum(last_5m):sum:trace.servlet.request.errors{env:cohort,service:easytravel-backend}.as_count() / sum:trace.servlet.request.hits{env:cohort,service:easytravel-backend}.as_count() * 100 > 5`. Alert 5, Warning 2, name `[u<seat>] Backend error rate above 5 %`, tags `lab:d3-303`, `u<seat>`, notify nobody.  
- **Action:** Create monitor B: **New Monitor \> Logs**, search `service:easytravel-backend env:cohort "CreditCardCheckError500"`, count over 5 minutes, alert above 10, name `[u<seat>] CreditCardCheckError500 logs`.  
- **Action:** Create the composite: **New Monitor \> Composite**, `a && b`, name `[u<seat>] Backend errors - credit-card fault`. Read the states of A, B and the composite while the fault is on (allow about 4 minutes).  
- **Action:** Complete `evidence_D3_3.json`. At the end delete the composite first, then A and B.

#### C. Action Items to Solve

1. Record the broken query, its status and the two defects.  
2. Paste your corrected query for monitor A and the evidence from Metrics Explorer.  
3. Record the IDs and states of A, B and the composite while the fault is on.  
4. Explain why the composite is better than A alone for paging.  
5. Fill the JSON file and call your instructor.

---

## 4\. Sign-Off Rules

| \# | Rule | S1 (self-check by script, then instructor) | S2 (instructor, in the browser) | S3 (instructor, in the browser) |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1 | Culprit identified | Host `web-prod-04` named | Top failing process named | Broken monitor and its two defects named |
| 2 | Method used | `rex field=_raw` used | `fetch logs ... summarize` by `dt.process.name` | Corrected ratio query on `env:cohort` |
| 3 | Pattern / evidence | `ERR-[0-9]{4}` pattern | Dominant error type `CreditCardCheckError500` with `ErrorCount` | `trace.servlet.request.errors` used with `sum(last_5m)` |
| 4 | Second view | `timechart` of the codes | Failed spans / timeseries and Logs-app count agree | Metrics Explorer proves the wrong environment |
| 5 | Complete | `transaction session_id` sessions; no `<<FILL_...>>` | Queries, counts and next action present; no `<<FILL_...>>` | Composite `A && B` created and states read; no `<<FILL_...>>` |
